re-extraction.csv lines 15, 31, 40 and 78 (Koizumi 2018: R2 elasticity at week 12, R1 roughness at weeks 6 and 12, hydration at week 12). These are the only rows for the three trials. Genovese and Czajka have no rows in re-extraction.csv, which was confirmed by grepping the trial column and the product and sponsor names. corrections.csv E6 (genovase 2017), E7 (koizuma 2018) and E9 (czaka 2018). All were checked against the PDFs in blind-papers: Koizumi Table 2 (p. 401), Genovese Results (p. 150), and Czajka section 3.2 and the Fig. 2 legend (p. 102). For every row, the SEM-to-SD arithmetic was recomputed and Hedges' g was recalculated. Koizumi: g = 0.93 (0.44 to 1.42), -0.10, -0.93 and 0.87, all matching the CSV. Corrections: E6 g = 0.35 (-0.01 to 0.71), E7 g = 0.35, E9 g = 1.42 (published version 9.44). E7's delta-method SDs (0.050352, 0.055328) were verified, and the same method reproduces the 9.167 and 7.70 cited for the hydration row. Agreed count of 46 = 24 inputs (n, mean, SD for both arms × 4 rows) + 4 g values + 18 corrected n, mean and SD values in E6, E7 and E9. Every mean and n matches the paper and the blind extraction exactly. SEM is the right scale every time (Koizumi Table 2 footnote, Genovese Statistics, Czajka Fig. 2 legend). Arm assignment, time points and source citations are all correct. Sign check: roughness rows 31 and 40 report g as -0.10 and -0.93, i.e. collagen minus control. That matches the roughness sheet's own stated convention ('negative = favours collagen', as in the Callegari rows) and Batool's roughness analysis. It does not match the task brief's 'positive favours collagen'. This is consistent within the audit, so it is not counted as a discrepancy, but anyone pooling these rows across sheets needs to know about it. Caveats raised by the blind extractor that the audit already handles or that do not affect values: (1) Genovese and Czajka measure elasticity as Young's modulus, where higher arguably means stiffer skin. E6 follows the authors' direction and says so in its notes. (2) Czajka's arms differed at baseline (7.9 vs 6.9, P<.05). E9 says it uses an endpoint comparison plus a sensitivity analysis that removes the baseline difference. (3) Czajka's subgroup n values disagree between the text and the figure (45/16 vs 44/17). The audit does not use the subgroups. (4) In Genovese the between-group difference at day 90 was not significant, which fits the corrected g with a CI that crosses zero (-0.01 to 0.71).

discrepancies.field: effect-size basis for R2 gross elasticity at week 12 (the same paper cells give different g in the two audit files)
discrepancies.audit_value: E7: derived endpoints, collagen 37/0.761536/0.050352 vs placebo 34/0.742904/0.055328 (baseline × (1 + % change), with delta-method SD), g = 0.35 (-0.12 to 0.82). Line 15: % change 37/4.32/3.248 vs 34/0.938/3.948 (SEM × sqrt(n)), g = 0.93 (0.44 to 1.42)
discrepancies.blind_value: Only % change from baseline is available: collagen 4.320 ± 0.534 SEM (n=37) vs placebo 0.938 ± 0.677 SEM (n=34); baselines 0.730 ± 0.007 vs 0.736 ± 0.008. No endpoint values are reported
discrepancies.evidence: Koizumi Table 2 (p. 401, mean ± SEM) gives raw baselines, then % change from baseline at weeks 6 and 12. No week-12 endpoint means or SDs are printed. Line 15 uses the printed cells directly. E7 reconstructs endpoints so they sit on the same scale as Grimes and Mahto's Data S1 entry, and its arithmetic reproduces exactly (0.730 × 1.0432 = 0.761536; delta-method SEM 0.00828 × sqrt(37) = 0.05035). This is not an extraction error. Both rows read the paper correctly. They differ because E7's endpoint SD contains between-person baseline variance and the change SD does not
discrepancies.impact: g for the same outcome differs by about 0.58 between the two re-analyses (0.35 in the Grimes and Mahto correction set vs 0.93 in the Batool re-extraction). Neither published claim is wrong, but a critic comparing the two files will see Koizumi elasticity at two different sizes. The audit's methods notes should say the gap comes from the scale choice (endpoint vs change), each made to match the form the original meta-analysis used. Also, baseline × (1 + mean % change) is only approximately the mean endpoint (the mean of a ratio is not the ratio of means). The bias is small here because baselines are tight (SEM about 1%)

discrepancies.field: notes: basis of the between-group t-test p-value
discrepancies.audit_value: Between-group p: 0.111 (t-test on week 12) and 0.035 (adjusted mixed model)
discrepancies.blind_value: Intergroup R2: two-sample t-test p=.111, GLMM p=.035 (data basis not stated)
discrepancies.evidence: Table 2 (PDF p6, journal p1151), R2 row: test 0.72±0.07 vs placebo 0.69±0.06 at 12 weeks, N=43/41. Footnote *: 'Compared between the groups; P-value according to the two-sample t-test'. The table never says the test was run on week-12 values. Running a two-sample t-test on the printed week-12 means and SDs gives t ≈ 2.1, p ≈ 0.04, not 0.111. The audit's own endpoint g of 0.46 (95% CI about 0.02 to 0.89) also excludes zero. So p=0.111 cannot be a t-test on week-12 endpoints. It was most likely run on change or % change scores (7.5% vs 3.0%).
discrepancies.impact: None on n1/m1/sd1/n2/m2/sd2 or on endpoint_g 0.46, which is correct. The note describes the paper's statistics wrongly: it implies the week-12 endpoint comparison was non-significant, while our own endpoint g excludes zero. A critic comparing the two would see a contradiction. Suggested rewording: 'two-sample t-test p=0.111 (basis not stated; inconsistent with the week-12 endpoints, so probably on change)'. No published effect or pooled claim changes.

discrepancies.field: sd1/sd2 (SD/SEM handling of Fig 1 and Fig 2 error bars)
discrepancies.audit_value: Unlabelled half error bars treated as SEM and converted, SD = half-bar x sqrt(22). Line 21: 0.080/0.078. Line 46: 11.82/12.95. Line 75: 13.74/10.46.
discrepancies.blind_value: Same half-bars recorded raw, with dispersion_type 'unclear' and no conversion. Line 21: 0.017/0.016. Line 46: 2.6/2.8. Line 75: 2.9/2.2.
discrepancies.evidence: The legends of Fig 1 (PDF p3, journal p812) and Fig 2 (PDF p4, journal p813) do not say whether the bars are SD, SEM or CI. The reported P values settle it. For R2 at 12 weeks, the difference is 0.0546. With SEMs of 0.0170 and 0.0167, the standard error of the difference is 0.0238, t is about 2.3 and p is about 0.03, which matches the printed Mann-Whitney P=0.035. Read as SDs, t would be about 10.7 and p far below 0.0001. For hydration at 12 weeks, the difference is 3.46. As SEMs, t is about 0.94, which matches the printed N.S. As SDs, t is about 4.4 and p < 0.001, which contradicts the printed N.S. The SDs this conversion gives (10.5 to 13.7) are close to the baseline Corneometer SDs in Table 1 (13.2 and 14.0). Both extractions agree on the raw numbers; only the blind extraction's decision to leave the bar type 'unclear' differs, and that is a refusal to commit, not a competing reading. The audit's sd_note already flags this as an inference and gives the 95% CI alternative (g 0.34 at wk4, 0.55 at wk12).
discrepancies.impact: None on the audit's g values (0.68, 0.18 and 0.28 stand). If the raw half-bars were used as SDs, as Batool did for line 75, g would be inflated: hydration wk12 becomes 1.30, about 4.7 times too large. This supports the audit's 'probably wrong' verdict on Batool's Yoon hydration row. The published claims are unchanged.

discrepancies.field: Direction of the ballistometer CoR parameter (source of 'higher = better')
discrepancies.audit_value: 'CoR chosen because its direction is defined (higher = more elastic recovery)'
discrepancies.blind_value: The paper does not state a direction for any ballistometer parameter; direction comes from the authors' 'improvement' language
discrepancies.evidence: Methods 2.9 (PDF p4) only says 'CoR is the coefficient of restoration'. The Table 8 footnote (PDF p8) says 'coefficient of restitution'. Neither says higher is better. Higher-is-better follows from the physics (more rebound energy returned) and from the results in section 3.5, which count CPNS +0.008 vs placebo -0.005 at week 12 as a 1.60-fold improvement. So the direction is well supported but inferred rather than 'defined' by the paper. The audit's wording overstates this a little and could say 'implied by the definition and by the authors' results'.
discrepancies.impact: None on the numbers. Week-4 CoR g is 0.05 (-0.34; 0.44), so it stays non-significant whichever way the sign goes, and the 'wrong' verdict against Batool's -0.88 (CPNS week 4 compared with CPNS week 8) holds whichever parameter is used.

discrepancies.field: sd_note: conversion of the digitised Figure 6B standard error of the mean (SEM) to standard deviation (SD), elasticity percent change
discrepancies.audit_value: verum +18.6%, SEM 1.9 -> SD 11.3; placebo +6.1%, SEM 1.0 -> SD 6.2 (SD = SEM x 6)
